Step-response characteristics

Source: R/diagnostics.R
ctrl_step_info.Rd

Compute the usual transient characteristics for each output and input case of a step response. Definitions (with \(y_0\) the value before the step and \(y_\infty\) the final value; when the model is known, a direct feedthrough jump at \(t = 0\) is not counted in \(y_0\)):

Usage

ctrl_step_info(response, sys = NULL, settle = 0.02, rise = c(0.1, 0.9))

Arguments

response

A ctrl_response (typically from ctrl_step()) or a model, whose step response is then computed.

sys

Optional model for the exact final value.

settle

Relative settling band.

rise

Rise-time fractions.

Value

A data frame with one row per output and case.

Details

  • rise time: time to go from rise[1] to rise[2] (default 10 to 90 percent) of \(y_\infty - y_0\), with linear interpolation;

  • settling time: the last time the response is outside the band \(|y - y_\infty| \le\) settle \(\cdot |y_\infty - y_0|\) (default 2 percent); NA if it never enters the band for good on the simulated horizon;

  • overshoot and undershoot: percent of \(|y_\infty - y_0|\);

  • peak and peak time: largest \(|y - y_0|\).

When sys (the model) is supplied the final value is its DC gain times the step amplitude (exact, for stable models). Otherwise the last sample is used and settled reports whether the response varies by less than the band over the last 5 percent of the horizon. Characteristics depend on these conventions, so state them when reporting numbers.

Examples

G <- ctrl_tf(4, c(1, 1.2, 4))
ctrl_step_info(G)
#>   output    case rise_time settling_time overshoot undershoot     peak
#> 1     y1 step u1 0.6607187      5.623333  37.23241          0 1.372324
#>   peak_time final_value settled
#> 1     1.645           1    TRUE
